question: I ___ him since 2019.
why: Since with a state that continues to now takes the present perfect.

question: You ___ see a doctor; that cough looks serious.
why: Should gives advice.

question: When I called her, she ___ dinner.
why: An action in progress at a past moment takes the past continuous.

question: She ___ in Pune for six years before she moved to Delhi.
why: Of two past events, the earlier one takes the past perfect.

question: If I ___ the lottery, I would buy a farm.
why: A second conditional (unreal present) uses the past simple after if.

question: The streets are wet, so it ___ last night.
why: Must have plus the past participle shows a strong guess about the past.

question: ___ honest man never lies.
why: Honest starts with a vowel sound, so an is used.

question: There is hardly ___ milk left.
why: Hardly takes any; milk is uncountable so many and few do not fit.

question: He failed the test ___ he did not study.
why: The second part gives the reason for failing.

question: In "Although the road was flooded, we reached school on time", the first clause is an adverb clause of
why: Although introduces a contrast with what follows.

question: This is the house ___ roof was damaged in the storm.
why: Whose shows possession: the roof of the house.

question: Which sentence contains a noun clause?
a: The man who spoke is my uncle.
b: We left when the rain stopped.
c: He ran fast to catch the bus.
why: What he said is the subject of surprised, so it works as a noun.

question: Passive of "The peon rang the bell."
a: The bell was rung by the peon.
b: The bell is rung by the peon.
c: The bell was ringing by the peon.
d: The bell rang by the peon.
why: Simple past becomes was plus the past participle.

question: They said, "We have won." They said that they ___.
why: The present perfect changes to the past perfect after a past reporting verb.

question: Passive of "Someone has stolen my bicycle."
why: Present perfect becomes has or have been plus the past participle.

question: He said to her, "Why are you crying?" He asked her why she ___.
why: A reported question keeps statement order and the verb moves back a tense.

question: He said, "I saw the accident yesterday." He said that he had seen the accident ___.
why: Yesterday changes to the previous day in reported speech.

question: Passive of "Who taught you to swim?"
a: Who were you taught to swim?
b: By whom were you taught to swim?
c: By whom was you taught to swim?
d: By whom did you taught to swim?
why: The subject who becomes by whom, and you takes were.

question: The word closest in meaning to "abundant" is
why: Abundant means present in large amounts.

question: The opposite of "ancient" is
why: Ancient means very old; modern is its opposite.

question: In "She sings very good", the word that is wrong is
why: An adverb is needed to describe sings: well.

question: Which arrangement is correct? Words: hard / success / comes / work / to / those / who
a: Success those who comes to work hard
b: Success comes to those who work hard
c: Success comes who work to those hard
d: Hard success comes those to who work
why: Only the first order makes a meaningful, grammatical sentence.

question: "To bite the bullet" means to
c: face a painful situation with courage
why: The idiom describes enduring something unpleasant bravely.

question: The new policy will ___ thousands of farmers.
why: Affect is the verb meaning to influence; effect is a noun here.

c: a long description of the seller

c: Date, time, venue, who may donate and a contact person
why: A notice must answer what, when, where, who and whom to contact.

why: Formal letters use Dear Sir or Sir.

question: A newspaper report of an event is usually written in the ___ tense.
why: The event has already happened.

question: Which is the right order for a newspaper report?
why: A report opens with the headline, then the writer's name, then the facts.

question: Which closing line is best for a complaint letter to a dealer?
a: I request you to replace the set within seven days, failing which I shall approach the consumer forum.
b: Fix it or I will ruin you.
why: It is firm, polite and states a deadline and consequence.

question: A job application letter that replies to an advertisement should begin by
b: referring to the advertisement and the post
why: The first line links the letter to the advertisement.
